a80.titolo: The Gemini app is now available on lower-memory Android devices.
a80.testo: The Gemini app is now available on lower-memory Android devices. For hundreds of millions of people globally, a lower-memory Android device is their everyday connection to the internet, education, and business. Until recently, hardware limits meant those phones only had basic voice commands. Now, we’re bringing the Gemini app to eligible Android (Go edition) devices, putting Google’s personal AI assistant in the hands of hundreds of millions more people. We re-architected the app so the core Gemini experience runs smoothly on hardware with less memory. Instead of typing out long prompts, you can talk things through or practice for an interview out loud in more than 45 languages with Gemini Live, point your camera at notes or forms to learn and translate, or create custom images with Nano Banana — like a flyer for a weekend bakery sale. To get started, download the Gemini app on Google Play, press and hold the power button on supported phones, or look for it preloaded on upcoming devices from partners like Transsion.

a90.titolo: Google Gemini App is Now Available on Android Go Devices With Lower Memory

a79.testo: Genie 4 is now available Earlier this year we introduced Project Genie, an experimental research prototype that lets you generate and explore interactive worlds. Early testers told us they wanted deeper control over what happens inside those worlds, and easier ways to build and share them. So today, we are rolling out a new Project Genie experience to eligible Google AI Ultra subscribers, making these worlds far more responsive, creative, and social. This update unlocks first-time access to Genie 4, new upgrades to Genie 3, the Project Genie agent which helps users build their vision, and a community gallery to discover, explore, and remix worlds. Project Genie brings together our most advanced world models alongside our Gemini models, empowering you to generate, step inside, and shape worlds directly from your browser. Experience Genie 4 in Project Genie With Genie 4, our most realistic and interactive world model yet, you can now prompt mid-session to change the world you created. Just type a new prompt while you navigate your world and you can edit your environments in real time. Shift the weather, drop in a character, or redirect the action. For the first time, Genie 4 pairs these visuals with real-time native audio that adapts as the scene unfolds, from ambient soundscapes to character dialogue. Discover new Genie 3 capabilities While Genie 4 delivers our highest-fidelity visuals, physics, and native audio, Genie 3 remains available in Project Genie’s model picker when you want longer runs or panorama-seeded spaces. a136.titolo: Google’s AI feature in Search gets its own incognito mode
a136.testo: Google’s search engine has long offered an incognito mode for all those search queries you don’t want logged or associated with your account. Now, Google’s AI Mode in Search is getting a similar feature. In a blog post, the company announced a new feature that brings “temporary threads” to AI Mode, where the conversations you have won’t be resurfaced later in areas like your search history or recommendations. Many leading AI chatbots already offer the option for temporary chats, Google Gemini included. However, there was not yet an option to have a temporary chat when you’re searching Google and are dropped into its conversational interface, known as AI Mode. Google says that users won’t have to adjust their settings to take advantage of the new option. Instead, they’ll be able to click a temporary threads icon in the upper right corner of AI Mode to engage in a temporary chat. This essentially works the same as a temporary chat would in the stand-alone Gemini chatbot. The option could be convenient to use at those times when you start digging deeper into a particular topic via AI Mode and realize that you don’t want the discussion to become a part of your search history because of its personal nature. Once the temporary thread is started, the session becomes detached from your account, Google says. This means that the responses the AI provides won’t be informed by past preferences, nor will they impact future personalization. That could also be useful for those times when you want to learn about something as more of a one-off, but don’t want Google to start to think of the topic as one of your main interests. u2a125.titolo: Superhuman pushes its Go assistant everywhere
u2a125.testo: Productivity apps are simultaneously trying to feed more context to their AI tools while also making those AI assistants available in every nook and corner of their products. Superhuman (formerly Grammarly) is going in the same direction with the rollout of features, including a personalized Go assistant, making agents available in Docs, and third-party agent integrations. While some of the company’s AI features have faced criticism, Superhuman started pushing its Go assistant after its rebranding last year. With the new rollout, it is making Go learn context across different apps and give better personalized suggestions for prompts. Superhuman is revamping its onboarding flow to let users connect their preferred tools and load context about their work upfront. The assistant works inline with the cursor — just like Grammarly does — and also manages other agents. Superhuman is also making the agent proactive, which means it looks for your schedule, keeps an eye on your email, and even drafts responses. The updated Go agent also learns users’ writing styles and responds accordingly in email and Docs. The productivity company is adding 20 new connected agents, including DeepL, Legora, Amplitude, Databricks, and Blackboard, through its Go SDK. The company is also thinking about adding AI to different products, including Docs and Superhuman Mail. In Docs, all Go agents work natively, and you can set them off to work on different tasks in the background. Users can also set routines to trigger workflows based on events. Until now, Mail has used AI as its central tool, which is being replaced by Go. Users can also do enterprise search by using data from the company knowledge base and connected tools. Go also uses this context to form drafts and organize the inbox across Google…

u2a117.testo: Canva will now allow you to turn off its generative AI features. With this change, you can disable the graphic design platform’s array of AI tools, such as its AI photo-extending Magic Expand feature, as well as turn off the ability to generate images with its Canva chatbot. Canva adds an AI ‘off’ button You can also select an option to see less AI-generated content in Canva’s library. This toggle doesn’t turn off every AI-powered feature on Canva, however. That includes Canva’s background remover and its Magic Grab tool, which lets you select an object in an image and move it somewhere else. Canva says these tools will stay on because they “make everyday tasks faster without generating anything new.” The toggle still turns off many of Canva’s other AI features, including Magic Write, Magic Design, Magic Layers, Magic Edit, Dream Lab, Canva Code, AI Shapes, and more. Since Canva’s big push into AI in 2023, some users have expressed frustration with the influx of AI features and asked for ways to turn them off. Canva has only continued to expand on its AI-powered image-editing suite since then, by rolling out a prompt-powered editing update in April and launching its first in-house AI model, Canva Craft, last month. You can also now switch a toggle to see less AI content in Canva’s content library. Switching this option on means you’ll see human-created content first when searching through Canva’s library for templates, graphics, and other design elements. Canva says a “small portion” of its library consists of AI-generated content, and that any design that uses one of these elements will have an AI label in its metadata. u3a167.titolo: Moige contro Meta e TikTok: rinvio a gennaio 2027
u3a167.testo: Questa mattina era prevista l’ultima udienza del class action promossa dal Moige e da alcune famiglie contro Meta e TikTok, la prima azione collettiva inibitoria di questo tipo in Europa. Gli avvocati volevano chiedere un provvedimento di inibizione, ma il Tribunale di Milano ha rinviato tutto al 21 gennaio 2027 perché potrebbe essere approvate norme sul divieto di accesso ai social media. Rinvio basato su una norma ipotetica Il processo era iniziato a metà maggio. L’obiettivo del Moige non è quello di ottenere un risarcimento, come avvenuto negli Stati Uniti, ma l’obbligo di implementare misure efficaci per proteggere i minori. In dettaglio sono state avanzate tre richieste: - Una verifica reale dell’età per impedire l’accesso ai più piccoli - L’eliminazione dei meccanismi che favoriscono la dipendenza, come scroll infinito, autoplay e algoritmi progettati per trattenere l’attenzione - Informazioni chiare e trasparenti sui rischi per la salute, attraverso un vero e proprio “bugiardino” dei social Sui primi due punti sono già arrivate decisioni della Commissione europea, confermando la violazione del Digital Services Act. Meta non impedisce l’uso di Instagram e Facebook ai minori di 13 anni, mentre TikTok ha implementato funzionalità che creano dipendenza. Il Tribunale di Milano ha motivato il rinvio al 21 gennaio 2027 con la necessità di valutare le norme che dovrebbero essere approvate dal Parlamento (entro il 21 dicembre 2026), ovvero l’emendamento al decreto sicurezza che vieta l’accesso ai social media per i minori di 13 anni. Al momento questo divieto è solo sulla carta. Non è certa la sua approvazione, considerato che è identico a quello previsto dal KIDS Act.
